technical.summary: Short-term momentum signals (RSI9, MACD crossover, Hull flip) show bullish structure, but intermediate trend weakness (ADX 14.5, price below EMA50/200) and overbought conditions (StochRSI, Williams %R) limit conviction for a high-probability swing entry.

fundamental.summary: AAL shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and elevated earnings risk in 41 days.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear sentiment (24/10) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but weak congressional activity and absent news data limit conviction; neutral AAII reading suggests mixed institutional positioning.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (295.5) indicates extreme market stress, strong dollar pressures multinationals like AAL, and earnings in 41 days adds event risk.

debate.key_bull_argument: Short-term momentum signals (Hull flip, MACD crossover, three white soldiers) combined with extreme fear sentiment (24/10) create a contrarian entry opportunity near support at 13.64.
debate.key_bear_argument: Severe macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis, strong dollar), price trapped below both EMA50/200, overbought oscillators signaling momentum exhaustion, high earnings risk in 41 days, and zero fundamental conviction make this a low-probability swing trade.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term momentum signals (Hull flip, MACD crossover) and extreme fear sentiment (24/10) create a contrarian setup at support, but severe macro headwinds and overbought oscillators with 41-day earnings event risk make conviction too low for swing entry.
decision.primary_risk: Inverted yield curve + VIX crisis (295.5) + strong dollar headwinds create macro environment hostile to cyclical airline stocks; earnings in 41 days adds binary event risk that can gap through technical support.
decision.agent_agreement: moderate — technical and sentiment agents show bullish signals, but fundamental and risk agents strongly oppose; debate winner (bear) reflects macro severity outweighing short-term momentum
